evidence.quote: Father Brown followed them with his finger on the edge of the table, like a man trying to learn a tune on the piano.
evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown methodically tracks and analyzes the pattern of the footsteps.

evidence.quote: Father Brown had the kind of head that cannot help asking questions; and on this apparently trivial question his head almost split. He had seen men run in order to jump. He had seen men run in order to slide. But why on earth should a man run in order to walk?
evidence.paraphrase: Brown poses systematic questions to make sense of the anomalous footsteps.

evidence.quote: Father Brown began to ask himself with more exactness what the steps suggested. Taking the slow step first: it certainly was not the step of the proprietor.
evidence.paraphrase: Brown reasons step-by-step through possible sources of the sounds, eliminating candidates.

evidence.quote:
This large and subtle and (in
      the ordinary course) most profitable crime, was built on the plain fact
      that a gentleman
dress is the same as a waiter
dress. All the rest
      was acting
evidence.paraphrase: Brown explains that the whole crime rested on the identical appearance of gentleman's and waiter's evening dress.

evidence.quote:
every work of art, divine or diabolic, has one
      indispensable mark
I mean, that the centre of it is simple, however
      much the fulfilment may be complicated.
evidence.paraphrase: Brown articulates a general principle that complex crimes rest on one simple underlying fact.

evidence.quote:
The other stood gasping for a few moments, and then staggered back into a
      chair.
evidence.paraphrase: The thief reacts with shock when Father Brown names him.

evidence.quote:
They felt as you and I would feel if the inanimate world
      disobeyed
if a chair ran away from us.
evidence.paraphrase: The diners are startled that a waiter behaved unexpectedly, likened to inanimate objects disobeying.

evidence.quote:
his evening coat is green and not black.
      If (supposing that you have the star-defying audacity to address such a
      being) you ask him why, he will probably answer that he does it to avoid
      being mistaken for a waiter.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator frames the club's green coats against a normal expectation of black evening dress.

evidence.quote:
he contrived to lean against the wall just round the corner in such a way
      that for that important instant the waiters thought him a gentleman, while
      the gentlemen thought him a waiter.
evidence.paraphrase: The thief exploited the contrast between how waiters and gentlemen perceive the same figure.
